messages.content: The airline canceled Sunday’s 6:20 flight. They’re offering a 10:25 p.m. departure that lands at 11:58. Is that workable, or is there a better option?

The offered flight is technically possible, but it is a poor fit. With an on-time 11:58 p.m. arrival, you would likely reach the rideshare area around 12:20 a.m. and the Holiday Inn around 12:45-1:05 a.m. The hotel can hold the room for late arrival if notified, but that leaves little rest before Monday check-in. I found two nonstop alternatives with seats available: 4:45 p.m.-6:18 p.m. and 8:05 p.m.-9:38 p.m. The earlier flight is the strongest replacement; the 8:05 is still materially better than the airline’s offer.
Can they move me to the 4:45 without charging more? And is it still out of ORD?

Yes. It is an ORD-BNA nonstop, and because the airline canceled the original segment, it is available as an involuntary rebooking with no additional fare. Your Tuesday 5:15 p.m. return can remain unchanged.
Take the 4:45. Keep the same hotel and return.

The replacement is confirmed under the existing flight confirmation N4V7QC: Sunday ORD-BNA departing 4:45 p.m. and arriving 6:18 p.m. The Tuesday 5:15 p.m. BNA-ORD flight remains confirmed. There is no fare increase, and no checked bag has been added.
Update the arrival plan. I don’t need to check a bag.

After the 6:18 p.m. arrival, allow about 15-25 minutes to deplane and reach the rideshare pickup area. A downtown ride should take roughly 15-25 minutes in normal Sunday traffic, so the expected hotel arrival is about 6:55-7:20 p.m.
Do I need to call the hotel because the flight changed?

No. The new arrival is well before midnight and does not require a late-arrival note. The Holiday Inn & Suites Nashville Downtown - Broadway remains confirmed under HIN-736204 for November 3-5 at $548.26 total. Tuesday’s bag-storage and 2:30 p.m. airport departure plan is unchanged.
